summary: The note tells the story of Mary Patterson, a 45-year-old former schoolteacher from a Midwestern town who changed careers into tech despite stereotypes about age and gender. She taught herself coding through free resources, found community and a mentor, built a portfolio, and landed an internship and then a Junior Developer job. She now blogs and runs workshops to help other adults make the same shift.
one_line: Mary Patterson, a 45-year-old former teacher, breaks age and gender stereotypes to become a Junior Developer through self-study, mentorship and community.
key_facts: Mary Patterson is a 45-year-old former schoolteacher from a quaint Midwestern town who moved into a technology career.
In September 2023 Mary felt restless in her teaching routine and asked herself whether technology could be her calling.
In November 2023 Mary found an online community for tech enthusiasts, which showed her that the barriers she perceived were surmountable.
Mary began learning to code with free resources such as Codecademy and EdX, studying Python, Java, HTML and CSS.
She faced doubt from well-meaning friends and colleagues, and she turned to tech-focused support groups for women and online forums for encouragement.
In January 2024 Mary gained a mentor, Michael Johnson, a software engineer in his 30s who believed in inclusivity.
Michael Johnson reviewed Mary's code, taught her the culture and unwritten rules of the tech sector, and pushed her to contribute to open-source projects to build a portfolio.
Mary realized her teaching skills, such as classroom management, lesson planning and explaining complex concepts plainly, were transferable to tech project management.
Mary started a blog documenting her career transition and learning process, which became a beacon for others on similar paths.
Mary began job hunting in April 2024 and met skepticism over her atypical resume, but she secured an internship at a startup through a contact from one of her tech groups.
Her internship project won praise for creativity and user-focused design, and by August 2024 she was offered a full-time role as a Junior Developer.
Mary kept learning through Udacity and Coursera, studying subjects like AI and cloud computing.
Mary launched workshops for adults considering a career move into tech, covering coding basics and how to make the shift.
